raw_case_text:
A 65-year-old, Middle-Eastern male was admitted with a high fever, chills, and vomiting. The symptoms had begun while he was in Liberia, and he came back to Syria as soon as his fever worsened. The patient had no other clinical symptoms and no medical history of other illnesses or drug consumption.
A blood test was performed, and a blood smear was examined under the light microscope (Table 1). He was diagnosed with Plasmodium falciparum, and the test was run twice in two different labs. The patient was treated accordingly with artemisinin, 4 tablets per dose twice a day for three days (each tablet contains 20 mg artemether and 120 mg lumefantrine).
Twenty days after malaria treatment, the patient continued to suffer from fever, shivers, and general fatigue. Clinical presentation included pale skin, mucosa, and right hypochondriac pain without jaundice. A blood test with further lab examinations was performed (Table 2).
Blood smears were run for three consecutive days to detect Plasmodium falciparum organisms, while a computed tomography (CT) scan and abdominal echography were also scheduled.
The smears returned negative, and the CT scan revealed liver abscesses (Figures 1 and 2); thus, further tests were required.
A blood test was performed searching for Echinococcus granulosus antibodies and Entamoeba histolytica antibodies, and the test rendered positive results for Entamoeba histolytica.
The abscess was drained as a therapeutic and diagnostic measure, followed by a course of 500 mg intravenous metronidazole every 8 hours for 14 days (Flagyl), to complete the treatment. After improvement, the patient was discharged and instructed to contact his physician if any of his symptoms relapsed, which did not occur.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old Middle-Eastern male presented with high fever, chills, and vomiting after returning from Liberia, followed 20 days later by persistent fever, shivers, fatigue, and right hypochondriac pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed high fever, chills, and vomiting while in Liberia and returned to Syria as his fever worsened. After being diagnosed with Plasmodium falciparum malaria on peripheral blood smear and completing a 3-day course of artemether-lumefantrine (4 tablets of 20 mg/120 mg twice daily), he continued to experience fever, shivers, general fatigue, and right hypochondriac pain 20 days post-treatment.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior medical illnesses or regular medication use; recent travel to Liberia.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, shivers, vomiting, general fatigue, and right hypochondriac pain; negative for jaundice.

objective.physical_examination: Physical examination at representation showed pale skin and mucosa, right hypochondriac pain/tenderness, and absence of jaundice.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial light microscopy blood smears (performed twice in two laboratories) were positive for Plasmodium falciparum. At representation 20 days later, three consecutive daily blood smears for Plasmodium falciparum were negative. Abdominal echography was performed alongside laboratory panels.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT scan revealed liver abscesses. Serological testing for Echinococcus granulosus and Entamoeba histolytica antibodies was negative for Echinococcus granulosus and positive for Entamoeba histolytica.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Amebic liver abscess (Entamoeba histolytica) following treated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, confirmed by positive Entamoeba histolytica serology and negative Echinococcus granulosus antibodies. The patient underwent therapeutic and diagnostic abscess drainage followed by intravenous metronidazole 500 mg every 8 hours for 14 days, achieving complete clinical recovery without relapse after discharge.
